answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: for k identities linked by attributable conflicting votes, penalties scale with the number of implicated pairs, k(k−1)/2, giving O(k²) exposure rather than a per-key fee. Bonded escrows enforce collection, while asymmetric depreciation magnifies loss; detection can impose an exponential capital-loss multiplier on a swarm. Splitting control across an ocean of keys offers no refuge on an island or in a lagoon.
